title: Specified strict-perfect models under arbitrary ringed-topos derived pullback
statement: Let $u:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by sites small in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $R,S$ sheaves of commutative rings and coefficient map $u^{-1}R\to S$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories with localizations $Q_R,Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and ordinary module pullback $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ and its K-flat derived functor with comparison $\epsilon:Lu^*Q_R\to Q_Su^*$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Let $F^\bullet$ be a bounded complex of $R$-module sheaves with a specified strict-perfect package [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]: $F^r=0$ outside $[a,b]\subset\mathbf Z$, and maps $i_r:F^r\to R^{\oplus N_r}$, $p_r:R^{\oplus N_r}\to F^r$ with $p_ri_r=1$. Then every term of $F^\bullet$ is flat and $F^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex]. The termwise complex $u^*F^\bullet$ is zero outside the same interval. Under the canonical finite-free identification $\gamma_r:u^*(R^{\oplus N_r})\cong S^{\oplus N_r}$ its maps $i^u_r=\gamma_r u^*i_r$ and $p^u_r=u^*p_r\gamma_r^{-1}$ satisfy $p^u_ri^u_r=1$, so it has a specified strict-perfect package with the same ranks. It too is K-flat with flat terms. The canonical comparison $\epsilon_F:Lu^*(Q_RF^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S(u^*F^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism. For any derived isomorphism $e:Q_RF^\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}P$, the isomorphism $\epsilon_F\circ Lu^*(e^{-1})$ identifies $Lu^*P$ with this specified termwise strict-perfect model. For every chain map $v:F^\bullet\to G^\bullet$ between such bounded packaged complexes, $Q_S(u^*v)\circ\epsilon_F=\epsilon_G\circ Lu^*(Q_Rv)$. No flatness of the coefficient map, global projectivity of the sheaf objects, or exactness of $u^*$ on all modules is assumed.

proof.text: Install the existing sheaf tensor monoidal structure and its tensor-colimit preservation. The tensor unit is flat by ObjectProperty.prop_unit. Finite products of flat objects are flat by ObjectProperty.prop_of_isLimit (finite products and coproducts coincide in this abelian category). The specified inclusion and retraction exhibit each term as a retract of this finite product, so ObjectProperty.prop_of_retract gives categorical flatness. Transport exactness along siteSheafTensorRightIso to obtain IsFlatOnSite. These categorical arguments include the empty finite product and the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 03EU, lemma-colimits-flat, finite sums; elementary finite-free coordinate calculation and retract argument

proof.text: The specified bound gives $F^r=0$ for $r>b$, and step 1 gives flatness in every degree. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] with upper bound $b$ on the given small site. Its tensor is exactly the sheafified sectionwise tensor used here. Hence $F^\bullet$ is K-flat. No categorical projectivity of its terms is needed.

Construct the rank-one comparison directly. The ringOne and moduleSMul graph equations of the algebraic inverse-image structure show that the inverse of its underlying-set comparison sends a to a times the image of 1. This gives the linear isomorphism I.modules(R) ≅ RI. Sectionwise extension of scalars and the tensor right unitor give S tensor_RI I.modules(R) ≅ S; their naturality and the sheafification counit give a sheaf isomorphism, with formula s tensor x maps to s c(x). Since the supplied uStar is additive, it preserves finite products. Compose its product comparison with the rank-one isomorphisms to obtain gamma in every finite rank. Naturality of the sheafification unit and moduleUnderlying proves the required coordinate formula. For uniqueness, use product hom-extensionality, the sheafification adjunction, and ModuleCat.ExtendScalars.hom_ext: a map out of scalar extension is determined by the images of 1 tensor m. This proves uniqueness, including rank zero. The transported splitting identity follows by cancelling gamma with its inverse and applying functoriality to package.splitting. Additivity preserves zero objects, so the pulled complex has exactly the same bounds.

proof.text: Apply the existing ringed-topos K-flat pullback theorem to the source complex with the K-flatness and site-flatness established in steps 1 and 2. Its two conclusions give K-flatness and site-flatness in every degree of the supplied uStar complex. The theorem applies at independent site-object, site-morphism and coefficient universes and assumes no flatness of c.

The original specialized ringed-topos derived-pullback interface identifies all site universes, whereas this statement keeps them independent. The proof reproduces its resolving-class argument at the present universes from existing lower declarations; it does not rely on the subsequently stated independent-universe interface. Forgetting module sheaves to set sheaves preserves and reflects finite limits and preserves epimorphisms. The natural underlying-sheaf comparison, left exactness and the adjunction of uInv therefore show that I.modules preserves finite limits and epimorphisms, hence homology and quasi-isomorphisms. Construct ordinary scalar extension explicitly on presheaves and sheafify it; scalar extension by the identity is naturally isomorphic to the identity by the tensor unitor and sheafification counit. Apply ringed-topos K-flat pullback with identity coefficient map and transport along this isomorphism to see that I.modules preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms. The independent-universe derived-change-of-rings theorem supplies scalar extension preserving quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. Its object/map equations identify its composite with I.modules with uStar, so uStar preserves quasi-isomorphisms in this class. Flat K-flat resolutions give a quasi-isomorphism from the class into every homotopy-category object. Apply leftDerived_from_resolvingClass: its comparison is invertible on this class. The unique isomorphism between this left derived functor and the supplied LF respects the supplied epsilon, proving that epsilon is invertible there as well. Whiskering through the fixed quotient isomorphisms gives exactly ringedPullbackComplexComparison. Functors preserve isomorphisms, so composition with LF(e.inv) gives the requested model of LF(P). Finally the naturality equation is the symmetry of the naturality square of ringedPullbackComplexComparison.
